attempts.raw_response: The doctor nodded slowly, his expression grave. "He has already given his word, Colonel. As a gentleman and an officer, he is bound by it." The colonel stroked his chin, considering the weight of that single syllable. It was a fragile tether in such turbulent times, yet one that held immense power when wielded correctly. He turned to the guard standing stiffly by the door. "Prepare the carriage," he ordered, his voice cutting through the heavy silence of the room. "We shall transport him immediately. And ensure the path is clear; I will not have our prisoner subjected to unnecessary spectacle or interference from curious onlookers. His recovery is paramount, and so is his honor." The guard saluted sharply, turning on his heel to execute the command without delay.

pair.human_continuation:
"My dear sir," said the doctor, "the man couldn't move to save his
life--and he's asleep now."

"You must wake him up to move him, I suppose," said the colonel.
"But you may take him. Let me know when he's well enough to see me.
Meanwhile I hold you responsible for his good behavior."

"Certainly," said the doctor. "I am content to be responsible for Mr.
Carr."

"All right; take him and get out. Now for Whittingham!"

"Hadn't we better get the money first?" said I.

"Damn the money!" he replied. "But I tell you what--I must have a bit
of food. I've tasted nothing for twelve hours."

One of the servants hearing him, said:

"Breakfast can be served in a moment, sir."
pair.prefix:
said the colonel. "If he is, he's got only himself
to thank for it."

The doctor wisely declined to discuss this question, and confined
himself to stating that Johnny was not dead. On the contrary, he was
going on nicely.

"But," he went on, "quiet is essential, and I want to take him to my
house, out of the racket. No doubt it is pretty quiet here now, but--"

The colonel interrupted:

"Will he give his _parole_ not to escape?"

source_document.title: A Man of Mark by Anthony Hope
